title: Deterministic Replay & Auth Testkit for SDKs — Golden Trace Library
author: Priya Kannan
content:
Summary:
This document defines the deterministic replay and authentication injection testkit for Redwood SDKs (the "Replay & Auth Testkit"). The goal is to make integration tests for client SDKs and platform integrations reproducible across developers, CI, and release gates, while exercising auth flows, token rotation, and golden-trace comparison of outputs.

Audience:
- SDK engineers building language client libraries
- DevX reliability engineers integrating tests into CI
- QA engineers responsible for output quality regressions

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Provide a single, language-agnostic format for recording API interactions (requests, upstream model id, tokenization metadata, response chunks).
  - Allow deterministic replay with optional auth injection (simulate expiring tokens, 401 flows, refresh token rotations).
  - Provide golden-trace diff tooling for token-level and semantic differences to catch quality regressions.
  - Fit into CI: record on master, run replay in PRs and fail on regressions above thresholds.
- Non-goals:
  - Not intended to replace e2e UX testing that requires full UI and network stacks.
  - Not a load-testing tool (use benchmark suites under eng-serving-runtime).

Overview and architecture:
The testkit has three components:
1) Recorder: lightweight HTTP/SDK interceptor that captures requests and structured responses into a single Replay Manifest (.rdm).
2) Replay Server: deterministic backend that serves recorded responses to the SDK under test and simulates auth behavior based on an Auth Scenario file.
3) Golden-trace comparator: CLI tool that compares replayed outputs against a golden trace and reports token-level diffs, ROUGE-like summary metrics, and semantic embedding drift.

Key files and formats:
- Replay Manifest (.rdm) — JSON lines file with records: request, response, tokenization, model_meta, timestamps. All examples below use a compact spec (see example).
- Auth Scenario (.auth.json) — small JSON describing token lifetime, rotation cadence, and injected errors.
- Golden Trace (.golden.json) — canonical outputs with canonical prompts and acceptance thresholds.

Prerequisites:
- Node >= 18 or Python 3.10 for testkit runners (both supported).
- Access to the local Replay Server (docker-compose provided) or a CI-hosted instance.

Recording workflow (developer):
1) Install the recorder shim in your local test environment: npm install @redwood/replay-recorder or pip install redwood-replay-recorder.
2) Run your unit/integration test with RECORDER=on and RECORD_OUTPUT=./replays/my-feature.rdm.
3) Validate the manifest with: rdm-validate ./replays/my-feature.rdm.
4) Submit the .rdm and a matching .golden.json when opening a PR (see CI gating below).

Recording checklist: (table)
| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| request.path | yes | Path + method, must be stable (no timestamps in path) |
| request.prompt_hash | yes | Deterministic hash of preprocessed prompt |
| response.tokens | yes | Token list with token ids and strings |
| model_meta | yes | Model id, quantization profile |
| sdk_version | yes | SDK semver that produced the capture |

Example Replay Manifest record (single-line for .rdm):
{"record_id":"abc123","request":{"path":"/v1/generate","method":"POST","body_hash":"h1"},"model_meta":{"id":"redwood/fast-7b","max_tokens":512},"response":{"status":200,"tokens":[{"id":50256,"text":"Hello"},{"id":11,"text":", world"}],"streaming":false},"tokenizer":{"vocab":"gpt2-tokenizer-v1","normalized_prompt":"Hello, world"},"ts_recorded":"2026-11-02T17:03:21Z","sdk_version":"1.4.0"} 

Auth Scenario example (.auth.json):
{
  "scenario_name": "refresh-rotation-10s",
  "initial_ttl_s": 5,
  "rotation_every_s": 10,
  "inject_errors": [
    {"after_request": 2, "status": 401, "retryable": true}
  ]
}

Replay Server behavior and flags:
- Modes:
  - strict: only serve exact matching (request.body_hash + model_meta) records; mismatch => 409 (CI failure expected).
  - tolerant: fallback to best-match by prompt_hash (useful for dev iteration).
- Auth injection: load .auth.json, trigger 401s and token expirations per scenario.
- Latency simulation: per-record latency override to reproduce network jitter.

How to run locally (example with Docker):
1) git clone git@github.com:redwood/replay-testkit.git
2) cd replay-testkit && docker compose up --build -d
3) export REPLAY_SERVER=http://localhost:8080
4) python -m pytest tests/ --replay-server=$REPLAY_SERVER --replay-manifest=./replays/my-feature.rdm --auth-scenario=./replays/rotation.auth.json

CI integration (recommended):
1) Recording: Record manifests on merged main periodically and store in artifacts bucket (s3://redwood-ci/replays/<branch>/).
2) PR runs: Pull down golden traces and run replay in "strict" mode. Fail PR if:
   - token-level divergence count > 2% of tokens OR
   - semantic embedding cosine similarity < 0.985 OR
   - more than 1 unmatched request (409)
3) Flaky handling: CI will re-run the replay once; if failure repeats, tag as a potential regression and open a triage issue with trace attached.

Golden-trace comparator output (example):
- Summary: 120 tokens compared, 3 token mismatches (2.5%), semantic similarity 0.992 (pass)
- Token diff sample: 
  - expected: "the AI will respond with a greeting"
  - actual:   "the assistant replies with a salutation"
- Retain raw token ids in output to disambiguate tokenizer drift.

Acceptable thresholds (team defaults):
- token_mismatch_pct: 1.5% for generation models; 0.5% for deterministic outputs (embeddings, classification).
- semantic_similarity: 0.99 for headline-level, 0.985 for long-form.
- unmatched_request_count: 0 for strict mode.
(Teams may tighten thresholds per product surface.)

Auth test scenarios to include in CI matrix:
- expired_token_immediate_401: simulate immediate 401 for unauthenticated request; ensure SDK retries once with refresh token.
- rotation_under_load: rotation every 10s while serving 50 recorded interactions in quick succession.
- refresh_failure_then_recovery: simulate intermittent 500 from auth endpoint and eventual success.

Adding a new golden trace (PR checklist):
1) Provide .rdm (recording) file and .golden.json metadata describing acceptance thresholds.
2) Include rationale in PR description: why the golden is correct and how it was validated.
3) Add unit tests that assert the comparator passes locally.
4) Request reviewer from teams: devx + product owner.

Troubleshooting common failure patterns:
- Tokenization drift: differening tokenizer versions will change token ids. Fix: update tokenizer field in .rdm and run tokenizer-rewrite tool to map ids, or pin tokenizer versions in the SDK test runner.
- Environmental timestamps in prompt: prompts that include dynamic timestamps will produce non-deterministic body_hash. Fix: sanitize dynamic fields via recorder preprocessor.
- Model variant mismatch: recorded model id differs from allowed model in CI. Fix: add model mapping entry in replay server config (model_aliases).

Roadmap and next steps:
- Q1 2027: add per-token probability traces to manifest to enable ranking/regression detection.
- Q2 2027: integrate with Redwood Console for trace exploration and diff visualization.
- Long term: reduce friction for recording in serverless environments and add built-in model-compatibility suggestions.

Appendix A: Minimal Python example to replay a single manifest:
```python
import requests, json
REPLAY_SERVER = "http://localhost:8080"
with open("./replays/sample.rdm") as fh:
    for line in fh:
        rec = json.loads(line)
        r = requests.post(REPLAY_SERVER + rec['request']['path'], json={'__replay_id': rec['record_id']})
        print(r.status_code, r.text[:120])
```

Appendix B: Example comparator CLI usage:
$ rdm-compare --golden=./goldens/my-feature.golden.json --replay=./replays/my-feature.rdm --thresholds=./configs/default-thresholds.json

Appendix C: FAQ:
- Q: Can I use the replay testkit against hosted Redwood endpoints?
  - A: Yes, but only in controlled environments. Hosted endpoints may change; prefer private replay server for deterministic checks.

- Q: What about PII in recordings?
  - A: Recordings must be scrubbed before upload. Use rdm-scrub scrubber to remove emails, phone numbers, and customer data. See security-and-compliance/data-management for scrubber configuration.
